editorial.marketOverview: At 10:25 ET Nasdaq was down 3.93%, S&P 500 down 2.66% and Dow down 1.54%. Losses deepened from the opening; Nasdaq lagged S&P by 1.27 percentage points.
editorial.whatChanged: The decline broadened after the opening, but the directional regime is unchanged. Reuters also describes severe semiconductor losses; exact observation time is not available, so those figures are not used as synchronized quotes. Open Watch remains at 178 events.
editorial.marketInterpretation: Trade and AI valuation risks remain consistent with observed technology weakness. The prior inflation and growth releases remain relevant, but fresh policy pricing and paired yields are unavailable. Lower historical yields cannot establish current easing.
editorial.threeDayPath: Wednesday remains bearish unless a broad reversal develops. Friday's short session carries liquidity risk; Monday depends on semiconductor stabilization and weekend oil policy.
editorial.bullCase: A broad recovery of opening losses with improving chip leadership and falling volatility would challenge the bearish regime. Resilient GDP and AI demand remain potential support.
editorial.bearCase: Persistent cash losses and semiconductor weakness could extend downside through the holiday period. Tariff uncertainty and sticky inflation constrain policy relief.
editorial.watchNext: Verify QQQ, SOX, breadth, VXN/VIX, paired yields and oil; watch Beige Book at 14:00 ET and Friday early close. No new earnings catalyst independently verified.
